mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when unemployment exceeds 4%, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises and employment falls simultaneously, it indicates economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when both unemployment rises and employment falls, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rate negatively impacts S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during a tightening cycle, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when industrial production increases, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 250 indicates high inflation, leading to potential rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when CPI exceeds 250, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High demand (RSAFS) with constrained supply (INDPRO) leads to positive S&P 500 returns as growth outpaces supply.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when demand is high and supply is constrained, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, slowing housing starts (HOUST) indicate economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during late-cycle expansion with slowing housing starts, more than 50% of the time.
